The experimental design is well-controlled, artifacts and provenance are documented, and claims strictly adhere to empirical findings without overreach.

however, occurs when a single response misses the application' s deadline. Candidate-inflation latency
attacks drive the number of boxes entering non-maximum suppres sion (NMS) far beyond its clean
range. Recent evaluations report that realistic hardware, represen tations and optimized suppression

defended serving path. We therefore admit at most K candidates to NMS. The selection operation

Backend choice substantially reduces attacked
suppression latency, but no uncapped backend we
tested satisfies the declared suppression screen.
Following the deployment-realism concern of prior
work [
15, 16], we replay identical attacked can-
didate arrays through three suppression imple-
mentations. Over the same 48 images the sup-
pression call's p95 is 635.35 ms on the deployed
NumPy path, 177.71 ms on torchvision CPU and
49.08 ms on torchvision CUDA. CPU arms use the
host clock. CUDA arms are bracketed by device
synchronization after a warm-up, since an unsyn-
chronized timing measures the kernel launch, not
the work. The host-to-device copy is excluded; at
0.183 ms p95 it changes neither ordering nor ver-
dict, so the CUDA figure understates a backend
fed from the host.
5

evidence.excerpt:
Top-K selection is a standard operation and we
claim no novelty for it. What is proposed here is its
use as a deployment-selected bound on attacker-
controlled work, with the value calibrated against
a declared deadline and its accuracy cost mea-
sured. Let C be the candidates surviving the
confidence threshold and N = |C|. Before NMS
we retain only CK = TopK( C, K), admitting for
N > K the K candidates smallest under the
lexicographic key ( −sj, j): argpartition on the
negated scores at index K − 1 locates the cutoff,
every candidate strictly above it is admitted, and
the remaining places go to candidates equal to it in
ascending index order. The tie rule is not a formal-
ity, NumPy's introselect being unstable and exact
ties reachable at fp16 or quantized scores. The cut
is O(N ) and adds no pairwise IoU comparison, the
term Eq. (
4) bounds.

served deadline
The cap reduces client-side p95 under attack by
a factor of 15.10, a median over five independent
A/B sessions, yet the defended requests still miss
De2e = 33 .3 ms every time. That is no contra-
diction: the work bound applies to suppression,
and TNMS ≤ Dsupp does not imply Le2e ≤ De2e.
Nor is the miss attributable to the attack alone.
Attacked images must be delivered losslessly, since
re-encoding at the quality this pool serves did
not preserve the perturbation, so comparing them
against the JPEG corpus varies two things at once.
We therefore re-encoded the same 48 sources into
the attacked arm's format and served all three
arms through the same pool at the same cap, in
ten sessions of 144 requests at ϵ = 2/255.
The adversary turns out not to be necessary for
the miss. Clean lossless images reach p95 66.20 ms
at a deadline-miss ratio of 0.927, against 61.20

evidence.excerpt:
The anchor grid sets the maximum candidate
count, so a cap validated on one output tensor
says little about another. We repeated the capture
and the sweep on the same detector family with-
out its P2 head: 33,600 anchors against 136,000,
a factor of four in the quantity that sets the
ceiling. K = 1024 holds the suppression budget
on both, 3.11 ms against 4.19 ms in the same
run, while the runtime's shipped ceiling of 30,000
misses on both, at 187.30 and 342.96 ms. This is
suppression replay only; no accuracy claim is made
for the second model, and the bound is estab-
lished for the two geometries tested rather than
for anchor-based detectors in general.

out its P2 head: 33,600 anchors against 136,000,
a factor of four in the quantity that sets the
ceiling. K = 1024 holds the suppression budget
on both, 3.11 ms against 4.19 ms in the same
run, while the runtime's shipped ceiling of 30,000
misses on both, at 187.30 and 342.96 ms. This is
suppression replay only; no accuracy claim is made
for the second model, and the bound is estab-
lished for the two geometries tested rather than
for anchor-based detectors in general.

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: The defense is validated with held-out accuracy scoring, matched-format controls, multiple independent backends, a second detector geometry, a second corpus, and an edge platform under thermal throttling.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: The headline outcomes are established by client-scope end-to-end latency, deadline-miss ratios, worker stage timings, and held-out AP@[.50:.95] on VisDrone test-dev and BDD100K.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: The Top-K candidate admission bound and its deadline-calibrated selection rule are tuned against suppression tail latency and clean accuracy tolerance.

primary.claim_evidence_alignment: Claims match the experimental evidence closely and conservatively. Rather than claiming a universal defense, the authors show bounded candidate admission bounds pairwise suppression comparisons, precisely quantify the minimal accuracy cost (0.000188 AP held out), and demonstrate that image decoding dominates the remaining attack latency.
primary.evaluation_assessment: Evaluation includes controlled ablation sweeps over candidate budget K, perturbation budgets, backends, and format controls, reporting tail percentiles (p95) and deadline-miss ratios. Crucially, the authors evaluate their own proposed promotion criterion realistically, noting that while K=1024 bounds suppression latency, the deployed pipeline still fails end-to-end deadline requirements under lossless delivery.

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: Clean and attacked end-to-end performance was corroborated using independent client-scope timers, held-out validation datasets, multiple independent runtime backends, and decoupled hardware profiling.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Client-observed end-to-end tail latency, worker stage timings, deadline-miss ratios, and held-out detection average precision (AP@[.50:.95]) on VisDrone test-dev and BDD100K.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: Pre-NMS candidate selection thresholding and Top-K filtering calibrated via a selection rule targeting suppression tail latency and clean accuracy tolerance.

primary.limitations: The authors explicitly detail key limitations, noting that their algorithmic bound does not guarantee worst-case execution time (WCET), depends on session sample counts for tail quantile estimation, and cannot protect upstream pipeline stages like image decoding from format-induced overheads.
primary.method_assessment: The methodology is rigorous and clearly documented, separating client-observed, worker-level, and suppression-specific timing scopes. The authors replay identical attacked candidate arrays across multiple backends (NumPy, torchvision CPU, torchvision CUDA), architectures (server GPUs, Raspberry Pi 4B), detector geometries, and datasets while properly evaluating accuracy trade-offs.
primary.quality_rationale: This paper presents a methodologically thorough, nuanced, and self-critical systems investigation of adversarial latency in object detection pipelines. The experimental design is well-controlled, artifacts and provenance are documented, and claims strictly adhere to empirical findings without overreach.
primary.scoped_contribution: The paper characterizes candidate-inflation latency attacks on real-time object detection and evaluates bounding candidate admission before non-maximum suppression (Top-K) against declared deadlines. It also demonstrates through end-to-end breakdown that bounding suppression work alone is insufficient for pipeline deadline integrity due to non-suppression overheads like image decoding.

scholarly_quality.rationale: This paper presents a methodologically thorough, nuanced, and self-critical systems investigation of adversarial latency in object detection pipelines. The experimental design is well-controlled, artifacts and provenance are documented, and claims strictly adhere to empirical findings without overreach.
scholarly_quality.uncertainty: The authors explicitly detail key limitations, noting that their algorithmic bound does not guarantee worst-case execution time (WCET), depends on session sample counts for tail quantile estimation, and cannot protect upstream pipeline stages like image decoding from format-induced overheads.
